label: Rain and soil
title: Where rainfall and soil moisture disagree, Sep 2026 (experimental)
subtitle: Rainfall of the 3 months to Sep 2026 against root-zone soil moisture of Sep 2026; the gap compares both with 2015–2025
source: CHIRPS rainfall (Climate Hazards Center) and NASA SMAP L4 soil moisture, compared by Tinga Lens

categories.note: dry on the Rainfall tab and on the Soil tab

how: EXPERIMENTAL. Rainfall and soil moisture usually move together, but not always. This map shows the districts where they do not, and the districts where both are low. "Dry on both" means dry on the Rainfall tab (the driest 30% of 1991–2020) and on the Soil tab (the driest 30% of 2015–2025). The gap compares both measures with the same years, 2015–2025: it is soil minus rainfall, in standard deviations, after taking away the national pattern for the month (soil lags the rain at the start of the season, so most of Ghana shifts together). A district is flagged when its gap is 1.5 or more after that, and at least 1 before it. The pop-up shows both ranks and the gap.
limits: Experimental, version 0.1. It has not been checked against field soil moisture or crop records. A flag is a lead to look into, not evidence of drought or crop stress.

The gap uses the same reference years for both measures, 2015–2025, because the soil record starts in 2015. Rainfall in those years can differ from its longer record, so a district can have a gap even when its rainfall is normal on the Rainfall tab. "Dry on both" uses each tab's own rule.

Soil moisture is a NASA model product (SMAP Level-4) that is driven partly by its own rainfall estimate. Some disagreement with CHIRPS rainfall reflects two rainfall estimates differing, not the land itself.
Rainfall over the 3 months is paired with soil moisture of the last month because that pairing matched best in tests of 1 to 3 months.
Apr, May are not rated: in those months rainfall and soil moisture do not track each other well (the soil lags the rain at the start of the season).
Over 2015–2026 a flag appeared by chance in about 2% of rated district-months for soil drier and 2% for soil wetter. Only counts well above that mean something.

Flags usually form regional clusters (for example the north against the south coast), which points to the two datasets disagreeing over a whole area as much as to conditions on the ground. Do not read a flag as a problem in one district.
Ranks rest on only 11 reference years, so they are coarse. Districts that share a 9 km soil grid cell share a soil value.
Dry-season months, when normal rainfall is under 30 mm, are not rated.
legend_notes: Across Ghana as a whole, soil moisture ranks 0.8 standard deviations higher than rainfall this month. Flags show districts that differ from that.
Gaps come in regional clusters, not isolated districts. Typical gap this month: soil drier than rain suggests in Upper East, Northern; soil wetter in Greater Accra, Volta, Central.

Soil moisture: NASA SMAP L4 (SPL4SMGP), NSIDC DAAC
